Article Title: ‘Modi hell-bent on crushing democracy’: Kejriwal as AAP claims his residence turned into fortress
Article Text:
AAP alleges Kejriwal’s residence turned into fortress

BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi, Kejriwal’s associates of trying to destabilise country

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party supremo Arvind Kejriwal on Saturday slammed the Centre over the security crackdown in central Delhi ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) planned protest at Jantar Mantar, calling the situation “worse than the Emergency”.Reacting to the detention of CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka shortly after they arrived at Delhi airport from Mumbai, Kejriwal said the action showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi was "afraid of the protest."“This is worse than the Emergency. It's official… We are living under an absolute dictatorship ruled by Modi. Arresting cockroaches straight off their flight shows an unprecedented level of fear,” Kejriwal said in a post on X.“PM Modi clearly knows he only won the election through vote chori and now he is hell-bent on protecting his fraud by completely crushing democracy. Gyanesh must go, but so must Modi,” he added.The CJP had planned the demonstration to demand the resignation of chief election commission er Gyanesh Kumar over the Election Commission’s special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The AAP on Saturday alleged that Delhi Police had turned Kejriwal’s residence into a fortress ahead of the CJP protest.On Friday, Kejriwal had said that he and his family would attend the demonstration. He also urged young people to join the protest, which seeks Kumar’s resignation over allegations of “vote theft”.However, the detention of CJP’s key organisers and the extensive security deployment across the capital cast uncertainty over the planned mobilisation.Earlier, BJP president Nitin Nabin alleged that two groups, one led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and another comprising associates of Kejriwal under the CJP banner, were attempting to create instability in the country.“Today, an attempt is being made to create a highly dangerous and serious situation in the country. Efforts are underway to destabilise the nation, where 1.4 billion people are living in peace and harmony, contributing collectively to India's development. Who is doing this? Two anarchic groups: one led by Rahul Gandhi of the 'INDI Alliance', and the other led by Arvind Kejriwal's associates, CJP,” Nabin said.The BJP also hit back at Kejriwal over his allegations of electoral fraud. A party spokesperson asked the AAP leader to stop making such claims and referred to a Supreme Court decision cancelling elections to 50 municipal wards in Punjab, alleging that the AAP had rigged the process and prevented opposition candidates from filing nominations.“Stop this non sense Mr Kejriwal!” the spokesperson said, before asking Kejriwal to seek the resignation of Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann.The political sparring came amid heightened security in Delhi for the CJP’s planned ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ demonstration against the SIR exercise and CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
Article Summary: Arvind Kejriwal slams Centre over security crackdown ahead of Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) planned protest at Jantar Mantar. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka detained shortly after arriving at Delhi airport from Mumbai. Kejriwal says action shows Prime Minister Narendra Modi is "afraid of the protest"

Article Title: 'Anarchists have failed, planned to hold Delhi hostage': BJP slams Jantar Mantar stir
Article Text:
He alleged that the protesters had attempted to hold the country and the national capital hostage and were seeking to create violence.

NEW DELHI: BJP MP Sambit Patra on Saturday termed the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) proposed protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar a "flop show". The BJP MP claimed that the "anarchists" who wanted to hold Delhi "hostage" have failed."Jantar Mantar's story is not India's story. What is happening at Jantar Mantar, what you can see on TV and a few social media handles, is not India's story. India is calm and going ahead under good governance. We have been seeing that a few anarchist forces have been spreading anarchy in a corner of Delhi for the past few days. But today the anarchists have failed. The flop show of anarchist elements has completely collapsed. There was an attempt to hold India, the national capital, captive; that there be arson here, that there be violence here. But today, 'loktantra' has triumphed over bheedtantra," the BJP MP said.He alleged that the protesters had attempted to hold the country and the national capital hostage and were seeking to create violence."They were trying to hold India hostage, make the national capital hostage. They wanted violence," he said.The remarks came amid a political row over the CJP's proposed demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The outfit had called the protest over allegations of voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and changes relating to Form 6, which is used for voter registration.Earlier on Saturday, the CJP claimed that its leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police from inside an aircraft after it landed in the national capital. The leaders had travelled from Mumbai to attend the planned demonstration.In a video shared by the outfit, Dipke accused the police of preventing them from disembarking and described the alleged action as dictatorship. Police personnel reportedly told the leaders that they did not have permission to hold the protest at Jantar Mantar.Police sources told news agency PTI that the three leaders were taken to different locations, with Dipke taken to Gurugram, Ranka to Dwarka in Delhi and Das to another location in the city.The developments came as BJP president Nitin Nabin separately accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal and the CJP of attempting to create anarchy and destabilise the country. He alleged that their actions were driven by political ambitions and claimed that they were acting in collusion with foreign forces, charges that the opposition leaders have not been shown responding to in the statements provided.
Article Summary: BJP MP Sambit Patra termed the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) proposed protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar a "flop show" He alleged that the protesters had attempted to hold the country and the national capital hostage and were seeking to create violence.

Article Title: 'Our Gen Z deserves better than Emer-GenZ': Shashi Tharoor slams 'war-like deployment' of cops for CJP protest
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor criticised the heavy security deployment and restrictions in Delhi ahead of the CJP protest, saying Gen Z deserved better

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Saturday criticised the heavy security deployment across Delhi in the wake of Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest against the Election Commission , describing the arrangements as “war-like” and questioning the restrictions imposed on citizens seeking to demonstrate peacefully.In a post, Tharoor said he had returned to the national capital after 2am and had “rarely seen anything like” the situation unfolding in Delhi, citing checkpoints, concrete barriers, spike strips, the deployment of 22,000 police and paramilitary personnel, cancellation of 250 trains and closure of 45 metro stations. He also referred to reports of young people being detained from their homes and streets in and around Delhi.Tharoor criticised the suspension of internet services in central Delhi, calling it the “most regressive (as well as repressive)” measure. He said freedom of movement had been “completely shackled” and pointed out that Jantar Mantar had been designated as a place where citizens could voice dissent in the heart of the capital.“One is entitled to ask where this extraordinary manpower and urgency disappear when women in our capital need protection,” he said.Questioning what would happen if protesters returned on Monday, Tharoor said those detained would have to be released. “Our GenZ deserves better than an undeclared Emer-GenZ,” he added.Tharoor argued that a government confident in the fairness of elections should welcome questions about the electoral process rather than respond with heavy security measures. “The government should provide answers, not lathis; expression, not repression,” he said.He also said barricades would not restore public faith in the Election Commission and urged the poll body to answer questions raised by citizens. Calling the situation “utterly shameful and unconscionable”, Tharoor said a democracy’s strength was measured by how it treated those who questioned its functioning.Several demonstrators were detained by Delhi Police after gathering at Jantar Mantar amid extensive barricading and heightened security.The CJP had called for a protest over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and demanded Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Police had denied permission for the demonstration, citing security considerations and procedural requirements.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor criticised the heavy security deployment across Delhi in the wake of Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest against the Election Commission. He described the arrangements as ‘war-like’ and questioned the restrictions imposed on citizens seeking to demonstrate peacefully.

Article Title: Who will lead CJP protest? Abhijeet Dipke names Ajinkya Shinde in pre-recorded video
Article Text:
Cockroach Janta Party names Ajinkya Shinde to lead its Jantar Mantar protest after founder Abhijeet Dipke and two associates are detained at Delhi airport. (Abhijeet Dipke, Ajinkya Shinde)

Security tightened across Delhi

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Saturday named its organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde to lead its protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi after founder Abhijeet Dipke, along with Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, was detained by Delhi Police at the airport.The party shared a pre-recorded video of Dipke, which he had filmed on Friday night in anticipation of a possible arrest ahead of the proposed October 10 demonstration demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.Also read: CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka detained from Delhi airport ahead of Jantar Mantar protest "Until Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are in detention, CJP’s Organization In-Charge Ajinkya Shinde will lead this protest at Jantar Mantar. Abhijeet had pre-recorded this video last night in anticipation of a potential arrest."The development came as security was tightened across the national capital ahead of the CJP's proposed protest. Delhi Police had denied permission for the demonstration, citing law and order concerns and the possibility of inconvenience to residents.Dipke had earlier said he was prepared to face arrest while travelling to Delhi for the protest. He accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah of using security restrictions to prevent people from joining the demonstration.At least 1500 people had been detained under Section 65 of the Delhi Police Act as authorities stepped up security ahead of the planned demonstration.Traffic restrictions came into force at 6 am, with diversions planned at several locations across the city. Police personnel were deployed at barricades and key intersections to check vehicles and monitor movement around the protest site.The Delhi Traffic Police warned of possible disruptions around Connaught Place, Mandi House, Jantar Mantar, Patel Chowk and other major intersections in central Delhi.The affected stretches included the Ashoka Road-Jantar Mantar Road roundabout, Tolstoy Marg-Janpath crossing, Jai Singh Road-Sansad Marg crossing, Rail Bhawan roundabout, Patel Chowk, Gol Dak Khana and Windsor Place.In its communication to CJP, Delhi Police said the party's intimation did not qualify as a duly filed application for permission. Police guidelines require applications for demonstrations at Jantar Mantar to be submitted at least 10 days in advance.Authorities also cited alleged past violations of protest conditions, including demonstrations continuing beyond the stipulated time limits.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) named organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde to lead its protest at Jantar Mantar. Party founder Abhijeet Dipke, along with Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, was detained by Delhi Police at the airport. Delhi Police had denied permission for the demonstration, citing law and order concerns and the possibility of inconvenience.

Article Title: What’s happening at Jantar Mantar? CJP’s ‘cockroaches’ grounded before anti-SIR showdown
Article Text:
‘Not even Indira Gandhi did this’: CJP founder alleges police boarded flight to detain leaders

CJP leaders detained inside aircraft

YouTuber Dhruv Rathee detained ahead of protest

35,000 personnel deployed; internet curbs & traffic restrictions

Liquor shops shut, commercial activity affected

Rahul backs demand for CEC’s removal, but Congress skips protest

CJP appeals for peace amid police restrictions

NEW DELHI: As planned, the ‘cockroaches’ could not make their way to Jantar Mantar, with the detention of key Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders before they could reach the protest site throwing the outfit’s ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ plans into disarray. Delhi’s sweeping security crackdown, which has reportedly led to over 1,500 detentions across the capital, further dampened the expected turnout at the demonstration against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police upon arriving at Indira Gandhi International airport from Mumbai.The outfit’s head of legal affairs, Ratna Singh, was also detained.The developments came hours before the outfit’s planned ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ demonstration demanding the removal of Gyanesh Kumar over the Election Commission’s special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The protest, proposed by the CJP despite Delhi Police denying permission, was expected to draw around 20,000 participants. However, the detention of key organisers and the extensive security deployment have majorly affected preparations for the demonstration.In a video shared on social media, Dipke could be heard alleging that Delhi Police personnel entered the aircraft shortly after it landed to detain him and his fellow leaders.“So, you can see that Delhi Police is entering the plane to arrest us. They are all entering the plane. We just landed. All the Delhi Police officers are standing in the aisle. They are trying to arrest us from inside the plane. The entire Delhi Police is getting on the plane. This is the fear of Narendra Modi,” Dipke said.“Not even Indira Gandhi did this during the Emergency. All we wanted to do is a peaceful protest, and they are picking us up from the flight like we are criminals,” he added.In the same video, CJP leaders Ranka and Das could be heard raising slogans of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai” and “Inquilab Zindabad”.The group termed the detentions "illegal" and alleged that the police action was aimed at preventing its leaders from reaching Jantar Mantar for the planned demonstration.Almost an hour before the CJP leadership arrived at Delhi airport, the outfit’s supporter and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was reportedly detained by Gurugram Police from his residence in Sector 56.Rathee, who lives abroad, had travelled to participate in the demonstration, according to the information shared by the outfit. His reported detention added to the uncertainty surrounding the protest, which had already triggered heightened security arrangements across Delhi and its adjoining areas.Delhi was placed under an extensive security blanket ahead of the proposed mobilisation. Around 35,000 police personnel were deployed, with Central Police personnel also present in large numbers around Jantar Mantar and other key locations.The security arrangements included CCTV surveillance and body cameras fitted to the uniforms of deployed personnel.A section of Delhi Police was also designated as the “Pink Force”.Mobile internet services were scheduled to be suspended within a 4-km radius of Jantar Mantar. Authorities also imposed traffic restrictions on roads along Delhi’s borders with Uttar Pradesh and Haryana, as well as routes leading to Jantar Mantar and other parts of New Delhi.Police were coordinating with cab aggregators to regulate vehicle movement, while several trains were reportedly cancelled. The measures formed part of the broader security plan to manage the expected crowds and prevent disruptions across the capital.The scale of the deployment, however, came amid allegations by the CJP that detaining its organisers before they could reach the venue was an attempt to prevent a peaceful protest.The restrictions extended beyond security and transport. Liquor outlets across Delhi were ordered to remain closed on October 9 and 10.Commercial activity was also expected to be affected in parts of the city, particularly around Connaught Place. Market associations in Connaught Place, Sadar Bazar and parts of Karol Bagh and Chandni Chowk confirmed closures for October 10.Markets in Green Park, Sarojini Nagar and Greater Kailash, however, were expected to remain open.The curbs and closures added to the disruption surrounding the proposed demonstration, with authorities preparing for a large turnout even as the detention of key organisers cast doubt on the protest’s eventual scale.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi reiterated his demand for Gyanesh Kumar’s removal, echoing the central demand of the CJP and other opposition voices opposing the SIR exercise.In a post on X, the former Congress chief wrote: "Gyanesh Kumar will go. This government will go. ""Then the repair of democracy will begin," he added, ending his post with the national flag emoji.However, the Congress stayed away from the CJP’s planned demonstration. Rahul travelled to Chennai to attend an event involving his ally and Tamil Nadu chief minister Vijay.Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal , meanwhile, had promised to attend the protest with his family. But the detention of key CJP leaders and the heavy security deployment threatened to reduce the gathering well below the turnout initially anticipated by organisers.Kejriwal criticised the Narendra Modi-led Centre over the restrictions, saying: “This is worse than the Emergency, we are living under an absolute dictatorship ruled by Modi.”On the day of its planned ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ protest, the CJP issued an appeal urging participants to maintain peace, avoid violence and vandalism, follow lawful instructions and ensure that emergency services were not obstructed.The outfit also called on participants to remain peaceful, alert and united. It described the demonstration as an effort to seek accountability over the Election Commission’s special intensive revision of electoral rolls.Despite Delhi Police denying permission for the protest, the CJP had called for a large mobilisation at Jantar Mantar.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police upon arriving at Indira Gandhi International airport from Mumbai. The outfit’s head of legal affairs, Ratna Singh, was also detained. Around 35,000 police personnel were deployed, with Central Police personnel also present in large numbers around Jantar Mantar and other key locations. Mobile internet services were scheduled to be suspended within a 4-km radius of the protest site.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) has urged Chief Justice of India to intervene in the detention of lawyers by Delhi Police and central forces, condemning the alleged use of excessive force against advocates protesting peacefully in the Supreme Court area.The association expressed particular concern over the detention of senior and young lawyers, including women advocates, and called for action on the matter.The CJI is understood to have communicated to the authorities to release the detained lawyers."The Supreme Court Bar Association resolves to request the Hon'ble Chief Justice of India to intervene urgently and take up the matter with the concerned authorities so that the whereabouts and safety of every detained advocate are ascertained, they are given access to legal assistance, and those against whom there are no lawful grounds for detention are released immediately. The circumstances of the detentions and the reported use of force be examined, and appropriate action be taken in accordance with law. A copy of this resolution shall be placed before the Hon'ble Chief Justice of India for urgent consideration," the statement by the Association read.Several lawyers marching from the Supreme Court towards Jantar Mantar were detained by Delhi Police on Saturday ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s proposed protest.The advocates, dressed in formal suits, raised slogans and carried posters demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation before police stopped them at barricades on Bhagwan Das Road near the Supreme Court.The detentions came amid heightened security across the national capital ahead of the proposed demonstration. Around 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across Delhi, while entry and exit restrictions remain in place at 45 metro stations.Surveillance has also been stepped up at the city’s borders, railway stations, bus terminals and other sensitive locations.Delhi Police denied permission for the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest, citing inadequate notice and concerns over compliance with conditions during an earlier demonstration.On Saturday, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police inside an aircraft shortly after it landed in the national capital. Around 1,500 people have been detained so far in connection with the planned protest.
Article Summary: Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) condemns alleged use of excessive force. CJI understood to have communicated to the authorities to release the detained lawyers. Lawyers marching from Supreme Court towards Jantar Mantar were detained by Delhi Police.

Article Title: Elon Musk fires another salvo over Starlink delay, targets Ambani again
Article Text:
Musk argued that Starlink could improve access to the internet in underserved parts of the country

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Friday fired another salvo over the delay in the commercial rollout of Starlink in India, taking swipe at billionaire Mukesh Ambani once again.In a post on X, Musk addressed the Reliance Industries chairman as “Prime Minister Ambani”, alleging that he was the “real boss of India” and questioning why Starlink was yet to receive the necessary clearances to begin commercial operations.“Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?” Musk wrote.He argued that Starlink could improve access to the internet in underserved parts of the country, particularly for children seeking educational opportunities and small businesses looking to reach international markets.“There are many areas of India, as there are in all countries, with no Internet access, which denies children the opportunity for education and for small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market. Starlink would change their lives for the better. Thank you” he added.Musk's latest remarks come a day after he accused unnamed Indian business groups of obstructing Starlink's entry to protect their market positions.He had alleged that the company was being blocked by “certain oligarchs” seeking to maintain a “monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people”.The Indian government has rejected the allegations, maintaining that the delay stems from pending regulatory and security requirements rather than preferential treatment for domestic telecom companies.At the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi, Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said India would not permit a monopoly in any sector and that three satellite communication operators had received licences.These include Reliance Jio Satcom, Bharti Airtel-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Starlink. Amazon's Project Kuiper has also expressed interest in entering the market and will undergo the standard evaluation process.Scindia said the government was finalising the satellite spectrum pricing framework, while security assessments by the Ministry of Home Affairs and other agencies were under way. Commercial operations can begin once the companies meet the prescribed requirements.The government has also said security clearances remain pending for all three licensed operators, rejecting the suggestion that Starlink alone is facing regulatory hurdles.
Article Summary: Musk addressed the Reliance Industries chairman as ‘Prime Minister Ambani’ He questioned why Starlink was yet to receive the necessary clearances to begin commercial operations. He argued that Starlink could improve access to the internet in underserved parts of the country.

Article Title: Game of one-upmanship? For fourth day in a row, INDIA bloc MPs hit the streets ahead of CJP's Jantar Mantar 2.0
Article Text:
With another CJP buildup in the making, the opposition parties perhaps don’t want to be 'missing in action' this time around

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For four days in a row, opposition leaders have hit the streets of the national capital, demanding removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls. On September 30, when the INDIA bloc announced its 6-point protest plan against the CEC, it mentioned one street protest in the national capital - a march by all its MPs to the EC office on October 6.But the script changed.The opposition MPs, led by the Congress, returned to the streets with a march to Jantar Mantar on October 7, to Rajghat on October 8 and to Rashtrapati Bhawan on October 9. The police went all out to stop the protesters on October 7 leading to a 9-hour standoff at Akashvani Bhawan where Rahul and Priyanka sat on a dharna, before they were forcibly removed. However, a day later the cops changed their strategy and allowed the opposition leaders led by Rahul Gandhi to offer prayers at Rajghat, Mahatma Gandhi's memorial. The leaders staged a sit-in to highlight what they alleged was "hijacking" of the country by Prime Minister Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and the CEC through a criminal conspiracy of "vote chori."On Friday, on the eve of CJP protests, the INDIA bloc MPs once again took to the streets, this time to Rashtrapati Bhawan to submit a memorandum to President Droupadi Murmu.The march, as expected, was stopped by the cops. The opposition leaders then sat on a dharna, this time at Vijay Chowk.The change in the street protests plan took even some of the INDIA bloc allies by surprise with some reports suggesting that allies were not happy over not being consulted. Not all of them were present for the extended street protests, leading to some uncomfortable questions about the INDIA bloc’s unity. Congress denied these charges.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said all parties of the INDIA bloc had been invited, but the decision and communication came late on Tuesday night. "Therefore, it was natural that representatives from some parties could not participate in it. Some media outlets are making unnecessary comments about this," he posted on X.So, what prompted this change in protest plan? Was it the success of the October 6 march to Parliament protest that prompted the new strategy? Or, did the looming Cockroach Janata Party’s October 10 protest play a role in extending the INDIA bloc street action?To understand this, let’s rewind to June-July when youth came out in large numbers in several cities in response to the CJP’s agitation demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister against NEET paper leaks.The CJP, formed online in May by Abhijeet Dipke in response to a remark made by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant using terms "cockroaches" and "parasites" for those unemployed who attacked institutions through social media activism and litigation.On June 1, Dipke announced the first CJP protest for June 6 at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The next day, activist and educator Sonam Wangchuk joined the online movement. On June 6, the CJP launched physical demonstrations at Jantar Mantar. On 28 June 2026, Wangchuk joined the demonstration at Jantar Mantar and started an indefinite hunger strike demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.The agitation peaked on July 20, when students and youth from across the country marched to Jantar Mantar responding to CJP’s call. The Delhi police resorted to using unprecedented force to disperse the protesters. The political parties, which till then stood on the sidelines, tried to enter the protests. The Congress, which had focused on Rahul Gandhi’s “Chhatron ki Goonj” till then, staged a surprise protest outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s residence on July 21 to make its presence felt on the streets. However, the fulcrum of the anti-NEET paper leak protests remained the CJP, and the government was forced to accept its demand for resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.With another CJP buildup in the making, the opposition parties led by the Congress perhaps don’t want to be “missing in action” this time around and leave the field open for the CJP. That could be one of the reasons why the INDIA bloc MPs have extended their stay on the streets.The Delhi Police have denied permission to the CJP for the October 10 Jantar Mantar protests citing short notice, past non-compliance with directions and concerns related to public safety, law and order and traffic regulation.But the CJP has announced to go ahead with its agitation. Abhijeet Dipke asserted that the protest would go ahead regardless of whether police permission was granted and said CJP activists were prepared to face arrest.Questioning the measures taken ahead of the protest, Dipke said, "What is this fear? Why are you this scared? You are scared of the youth in the country. You shut down trains, you shut down Metro, what should one do?"Earlier today, Delhi Police announced an unprecedented security clampdown on the national capital to prevent protesters from assembling for the agitation. The cops are also keeping an eye on over 200 content creators as part of the monitoring exercise. Police teams are examining online posts and messages relating to mobilisation, gathering points and the proposed demonstration.Later in the day, Supreme Court intervened and ordered Delhi police to ease some of the sweeping instructions to ensure that citizens, particularly those who have no intention of joining the ongoing demonstrations, were not inconvenienced. The top court said Metro and train services cannot be completely stopped and asked authorities to reconsider such restrictions in a proportionate manner.A bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also clarified that the present proceedings primarily concern restrictions affecting the movement of ordinary citizens and public transport and not the broader right to protest.While the government and security forces will be closely watching the CJP's mobilisation on Saturday, the INDIA bloc will also be keeping an eagle's eye on how the youth respond. In July, the CJP managed to draw large crowds, leaving opposition parties struggling to make their presence felt.This time, the opposition has taken to the streets even before the CJP's planned protest. The question now is whether the INDIA bloc can match the CJP's mobilisation or whether the youth-led group will once again draw bigger crowds. The October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar may offer some answers.
Article Summary: Opposition leaders have hit the streets of the national capital, demanding removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls. The opposition MPs, led by the Congress, returned to the streets with a march to Jantar Mantar on October 7, to Rajghat on October 8 and to Rashtrapati Bhawan on October 9.

Article Title: UPI vs credit cards: What should you choose for payments after MDR?

An often-overlooked aspect of credit card payments is that their value is not limited to rewards.

Value-back as rewards or cashback can change the economics

Transaction size alone does not determine the better choice

Does Transaction Size Decide the Payment Method?

Credit cards can offer value beyond the immediate transaction

The consumer's spending pattern should drive the choice

Before you tap, scan, or swipe: Check these 6 things

MDR may change the equation, but not necessarily in the same way for everyone

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

When it comes to choosing between UPI and credit cards, consumers should look at the overall value that they can derive from each payment method rather than the immediate cost of the transaction. While UPI provides convenience and simplicity, credit cards offer cashback, rewards and additional perks. With MDR on higher-value UPI transactions now being discussed, understanding the complete economics of a transaction becomes even more important.The overall value of a transaction depends on several factors including the payment mode, transaction value, the applicable MDR (if any), and the value-back attached to the payment method. This becomes particularly relevant as UPI increasingly intersects with the credit card ecosystem through RuPay credit cards.When a consumer makes a UPI payment from a bank account, the money is deducted directly from the account. While this offers simplicity and convenience, such payments generally do not come with any meaningful rewards, apart from occasional merchant-specific offers.A credit card changes this equation. The consumer can make the purchase today and get an interest-free period of 40-50 days, depending on the card's billing cycle and payment terms.Moreover, when it is a RuPay Credit Card that supports UPI payments, this flexibility is combined with the convenience of UPI.Credit cards are increasingly being designed around specific spending behaviours. Depending on the card, consumers can earn cashback or reward points on categories ranging from everyday purchases to high-ticket spends like travel bookings and electronics.Consider a Rs. 50,000 transaction on a card offering 5% cashback on the spend. The consumer could potentially receive Rs 2,500 back, subject to the card's terms, redemption value and applicable caps. Now if the consumer chooses to pay the same amount through UPI and the merchant passes on the entire MDR cost of 0.4% to the consumer, they will end up paying an additional Rs 200, making the product costlier for them, with no additional benefits.In fact, in most scenarios, credit cards can offer greater value to consumers through rewards, cashback and other benefits, without any additional payment processing charges being levied on them. However, this holds true only if consumers pay their credit card bills in full and on time, avoiding interest or finance charges. Once interest starts accruing on outstanding balances, it can outweigh the value earned through rewards or cashback, potentially nullifying the benefits of using a credit card.This is why comparing payment methods purely on the basis of transaction charges like MDR could be misleading. Rewards, offers and other value-back systems should also be taken into account. At the same time, a card may carry an annual or joining fee, impose reward caps, exclude certain categories, or offer a lower reward rate on certain transactions – which should also be considered.A common assumption is that UPI is best suited to small purchases while cards make more sense for larger transactions. However, in practice, the answer is more nuanced.Even a small Rs 500 transaction on a credit card could be more valuable than the same transaction through bank-account UPI if the card offers meaningful cashback or rewards on that particular spend. Conversely, a Rs 50,000 transaction may not necessarily justify the use of a credit card if the transaction falls outside the card's reward categories or has already exhausted the applicable monthly reward cap.Consumers should, therefore, look at the frequency of spending and the cumulative rewards generated over time. Small individual transactions can add up to significant value when they form a large portion of monthly expenditure. At the same time, card-specific discounts, cashback, merchant offers and reward points may add further value. Hence, the effective benefit can vary considerably across cards and merchants, irrespective of transaction values.An often-overlooked aspect of credit card payments is that their value is not limited to rewards. For consumers who manage their credit responsibly, the interest-free period can provide useful cash-flow flexibility. Some transactions may also be eligible for EMI conversion, allowing a large purchase to be spread across several months. Credit cards also come with issuer-specific offers, milestone benefits, travel privileges and more.But these benefits only have value when they are actually relevant to the consumer. Paying an annual fee for benefits that are rarely used does not necessarily make economic sense.Ultimately, there is no single payment method that will offer the best value for every consumer or every transaction. The important shift is to stop looking at payment methods only through the lens of convenience or transaction value and instead consider the net economics of the payment and choose the payment instrument that delivers the most meaningful value for one's individual spending pattern.The discussion around MDR on higher-value UPI transactions adds another dimension to this comparison. MDR represents a cost associated with accepting a digital payment, and the relative economics for merchants can vary across payment instruments and transaction types.The impact on consumers, however, will depend on how the ecosystem responds. If merchants absorb the additional cost, there may be little or no visible impact on the consumer. If the cost is reflected in pricing or an additional payment-related charge, consumers may have to pay it as part of the product’s cost.Whether and to what extent merchants pass such costs on to consumers is yet to be seen.
Article Summary: Credit cards are increasingly being designed around specific spending behaviours. Consumers should look at the overall value that they can derive from each payment method rather than the immediate cost of the transaction. Even a small Rs 500 transaction on a credit card could be more valuable than the same transaction through bank-account UPI.

Article Title: Patrón co-founder John Paul DeJoria turned a 96-acre Texas ranch into a home for more than 120 exotic animals; when it sold for $6.93 million, the buyer inherited the herd and a 2,700-square-foot unde
Article Text:
The ranch, known as “Patrón de Paz,” was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin.

A ranch that came with more than a house

The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms.

The underground shelter

The animals were part of the deal

Why DeJoria sold the ranch

DeJoria co-founded Patrón Spirits Company in 1989.

A 96-acre Texas ranch once owned by Patrón Tequila co-founder John Paul DeJoria came with an unusual combination of luxury, wildlife and an underground shelter. More than 120 exotic African animals lived on the property, while the estate also had a 7,540-square-foot main house, two barns, a stocked pond, a pecan orchard and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The ranch, known as “Patrón de Paz,” was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin, and stretched along 2,600 feet of Fitzhugh Creek. According to the Houston Chronicle, the property was listed for $7.495 million in 2016 after initially being put on the market for $7.99 million. It eventually sold for $6.93 million. As reported by ABC13 Houston, television director Jonathan Nowzaradan is the buyer of the ranch.The property was not simply a large Texas home. Its listing described it as an exotic-animal ranch, and the buyer was set to inherit more than 120 exotic African animals. According to the Houston Chronicle, the animals were part of the property when it was listed. The ranch included two barns, each with attached guest quarters, along with a stocked pond and a pecan orchard. As reported by The San Antonio Express-News, the animals included more than 120 exotic species and that the property was being sold with the animals and its furnishings.The estate itself covered 96 acres and overlooked Fitzhugh Creek, which feeds from Barton Creek. The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms. It featured wood-beamed ceilings, hardwood floors, partial stone walls and a large gourmet kitchen with a commercial-grade stove. Outside, there was a pool and spa, an outdoor kitchen and a wide porch overlooking the surrounding Hill Country.One of the property's more unusual features was underground. As reported by The San Antonio Express-News, the ranch included a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The Austin Business Journal also described the property as having a “2,700-square underground shelter.” So, when the ranch changed hands, the buyer was getting far more than a luxury residence. The property came with its land, buildings, underground shelter and a large collection of exotic animals.The exotic animals were among the details that made the ranch unusual in the first place. As reported by The Houston Chronicle, the new owner would inherit more than 120 exotic African animals. The ranch was a 96-acre property with a spa pool, limestone walls and the animals. The animals included species such as gazelles, wildebeest and antelopes.DeJoria, best known for co-founding John Paul Mitchell Systems and Patrón Spirits Company, had owned Patrón de Paz since 2008, as reported by the San Antonio Express-News. Realtor Dave Murray said DeJoria's primary residence was near Lake Austin and that he had decided to sell the Dripping Springs ranch. Murray also said DeJoria owned several other homes around the world and was selling four estates at the time. DeJoria co-founded John Paul Mitchell Systems with hairdresser Paul Mitchell in 1980 and later co-founded Patrón Spirits Company in 1989. The ranch's sale meant that its next owner did not simply acquire a large piece of Texas Hill Country property. The $6.93 million deal also brought with it a ready-made exotic-animal ranch, two barns, a creekside estate, a stocked pond and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter.
Article Summary: The ranch, known as ‘Patrón de Paz,’ was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin. The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms. The ranch included two barns, a stocked pond, a pecan orchard and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The new owner would inherit more than 120 exotic African animals.

Article Title: 'Nothing can stop India's youth': Chirag Paswan on metro, train curbs ahead of Oct 10 CJP protest
Article Text:
Union Minister Chirag Paswan

Union minister Chirag Paswan on Friday said “nothing can stop” India’s youth, as Indian Railways cancelled several Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive in Delhi ahead of a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar on October 10 over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls.Union minister and Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) chief Paswan, a BJP ally and NDA member, also said Indian youth could not be held back, questioning attempts to disrupt their movement. “These are the youth of India—nothing can stop them. To those attempting to spread such misconceptions, I ask: how many trains can anyone really stop? How much connectivity can be blocked? How many roads can be jammed?” Paswan said.Paswan has also sought to distinguish his position on the Election Commission of India (ECI) from an automatic defence of the ruling establishment. Amid the controversy, he had initially said being part of the Union government did not mean he would blindly defend anyone. He stressed that the ECI was an independent constitutional body and called on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to present a robust response to the allegations and address public questions to help restore confidence in the poll panel.However, days later, Paswan said he was satisfied with the ECI’s point-by-point clarifications and criticised the Opposition for what he described as “selective criticism”. His remarks marked a shift from calling for the poll panel to address concerns to endorsing its subsequent explanation.According to news agency ANI, Paswan also said on Friday that the Indian youth have the potential to lead the world, “they possess the capacity to show the world the way—just as previous generations have done—and so, nothing can hold them back.”The remarks come as the Railway Board has directed the cancellation at source of Mail and Express trains departing after 2 pm on October 9 and scheduled to reach New Delhi or Hazrat Nizamuddin stations between 4 am and 2 pm on October 10. Sources said the decision followed intelligence inputs and traffic advisories warning of severe congestion around the stations.Also Read| Chirag Paswan's UP gamble: Why PM Modi's 'Hanuman' is flexing his muscle against allies Paswan acknowledged that protests were a democratic right but argued that repeated demonstrations and road blockades inconvenienced ordinary citizens.“In a democracy like India, there is certainly scope for protests, and you should by all means protest. However, I want to understand this: if your sole objective is merely to protest, then go ahead—do it today, or even ten days from now. But protests alone will not yield a solution; dialogue will,” he told ANI.He alleged that Opposition parties were using the issue for political purposes and called on them to engage constructively with the Election Commission to address concerns over the electoral-roll revision.“If you have genuine concerns, go to the Election Commission; I am fully confident that the CEC himself would sit down to answer your questions,” Paswan said.The CJP protest is seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed gathering, citing short notice, previous non-compliance with directions, and concerns over public safety, law and order and traffic management.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke criticised the railway restrictions, writing on X, “Shut down the entire country if you are scared of the youth.”Trinamool Congress leader Derek O’Brien also targeted the government over the cancellations of the Howrah-New Delhi Rajdhani Express and Sealdah-New Delhi Rajdhani Express.“This is a big win for the youth of India and @Cockroachisback @abhijeet_dipke Bravo! Even before a ball has been bowled, the shit scared government has its knickers in a twist! (sic)” O’Brien posted on X.Meanwhile, Communist Party of India (Marxist) general secretary M A Baby has approached the Supreme Court challenging the restrictions ahead of the protest, including train cancellations and proposed metro station closures. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal is representing him, according to the party.Delhi Police has also urged the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation to shut 57 stations, while security has been tightened at several Delhi borders. The CJP has separately alleged that its national organisation co-in-charge Deepak Baliyan was placed under house arrest, a claim that could not be independently verified.
Article Summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan says Indian youth can't be held back. Railways cancels several Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive in Delhi ahead of a protest. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is protesting alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed gathering.

Article Title: 'City can't be brought to a halt': Delhi Police's rationale for restrictions ahead of CJP stir
Article Text:
The police also pointed to the limited capacity of Jantar Mantar, saying the site could accommodate only 1,000 people at a time. It said restrictions were needed to prevent overcrowding and protect protesters, residents, shopkeepers and others in the area.

Crowd management and public safety

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Police cite legal position on unauthorised protests

NEW DELHI: Delhi police has justified its restrictions on a proposed protest by the Cockroach Janta Party at Jantar Mantar, citing past violence, alleged assaults on women constables and the need to maintain public safety. The police said the organisers were proceeding without permission and stressed that the temporary curbs were necessary to prevent overcrowding and keep the capital functioning.In a statement posted on X, the force said, "The right to protest must be protected, but so must the right of a city to function safely. Responsible policing is about balancing both."The police cited violence during a protest in July to explain its concerns.According to the statement, permission had been granted for a one-day demonstration, but it continued for a month. More than 200 police personnel were injured, while over 2,000 people with criminal antecedents joined the protest, contributing to the violence.The police said the situation eventually spiralled out of control, leading to clashes in which students were also injured. It added that women constables had been molested and assaulted by protesters at Jantar Mantar in the past week.The police also pointed to the limited capacity of Jantar Mantar, saying the site could accommodate only 1,000 people at a time. It said restrictions were needed to prevent overcrowding and protect protesters, residents, shopkeepers and others in the area.The force said Delhi Police had to balance the right to protest with the safety of residents and the capital's economic interests. It added that the city could not be brought to a halt every time a demonstration took place.According to the statement, seeking permission allows authorities to estimate crowd numbers and plan traffic diversions, emergency access and safe movement around the protest site. The police said this would help demonstrators raise their concerns while allowing residents, workers and businesses to continue with their daily activities.The police said the Cockroach Janta Party was proceeding with its planned gathering without permission. Citing the Supreme Court's position, the statement said a protest held without permission was unlawful and participants could face prosecution.It added that organisers were responsible for explaining the legal position to those they invited to attend."The restrictions being put in place today are temporary. They are intended to regulate the flow of people, prevent overcrowding and keep protesters, residents, shopkeepers and others in the area safe," the statement read.The police said the precautions were intended to ensure that people could raise their concerns peacefully without compromising public safety or disrupting the functioning of the city.
Article Summary: Delhi police justified its restrictions on a proposed protest by the Cockroach Janta Party at Jantar Mantar. Police cited past violence, alleged assaults on women constables and the need to maintain public safety. The police said the organisers were proceeding without permission and stressed that the temporary curbs were necessary.

Article Title: Govt orders internet shutdown within 4-kilometer radius of Janpath–Kartavya Path ahead of anti-CEC protest
Article Text:
Security personnel keep vigil as part of heightened security arrangements by Delhi Police ahead of a proposed protests.

NEW DELHI: The government on Friday allowed the temporary suspension of internet services within a 4-kilometer radius around the Janpath–Kartavya Path crossing. The decision is part of the Delhi Police's preventive measures taken in view of the protests being called by various outfits, including the opposition Congres-led INDIA bloc and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)."Internet services will remain suspended within a 4-kilometer radius around the Janpath–Kartavya Path crossing. Services will remain suspended from 10 PM on October 9 to 10 PM on October 10. Instructions have been issued to suspend all forms of mobile internet technology," the notice said.Senior Delhi Police officers on Friday also held a high-level meeting at the police headquarters to review the law-and-order situation ahead CJP's proposed protest at Jantar Mantar.The meeting focused on assessing the security situation and reviewing arrangements to maintain law and order in the national capital, they said.Officers also examined recent observations made by the Supreme Court, which are expected to feature in the discussions, sources added.The planned protest has prompted heightened security preparations across Delhi.Of the 13 Delhi-bound trains cancelled by the North Western Railway for Saturday ahead of the protest, most are from Haryana.Though the railways cited “operational reasons” for the cancellation, the move comes ahead of the protests called by the Cockroach Janata Party and other groups in Delhi on October 10, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.On Friday, the Bikaner Division of North Western Railway announced the cancellation of 13 train services bound for Delhi.Delhi Police also proposed closing entry and exit gates at 57 metro stations across the national capital and reducing train frequency at these stations.Hours after the measures disrupting the railways & metro adopted, the Supreme Court orally asked the Centre to ensure that Delhi Metro operations are not completely suspended ahead of the protest, stressing that preventive measures should not cause inconvenience to ordinary commuters.A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana expressed concern over the scheduled closure of 57 Metro stations, observing that the restrictions could affect students, employees and other people dependent on public transport."We are concerned with closure of metro services," the CJI-led Bench remarked, addressing Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, who appeared for the Centre."One very important principle that we follow for every citizen is the principle of proportionality… You have to prevent certain things. Take measures only to the extent necessary to prevent them. But that does not mean you use a hammer to kill a fly. That principle must be kept in mind," CJI Kant further told Mehta.The solicitor general said he understands the concerns of the court and will discuss with the authorities concerned, but said that the remark of the CJI on use of a hammer was just an example and it should not be reported that the Chief Justice of India told the government that it is using a hammer to kill a fly.CJI Kant said, "Exercise caution in abundance. There is nothing wrong with that."
Article Summary: Government allows temporary suspension of internet services within a 4-kilometer radius around the Janpath–Kartavya Path crossing. Senior Delhi Police officers also held a high-level meeting at the police headquarters to review the law-and- order situation ahead CJP's proposed protest at Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: 'Repeal all assembly polls over last 2 years': INDIA bloc MPs meet President Murmu, make 4 demands
Article Text:
The opposition also demanded Kumar’s resignation

NEW DELHI: INDIA bloc leaders on Friday met President Droupadi Murmu and submitted a memorandum outlining four demands, as the opposition intensified its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.In the memorandum submitted to the President, the opposition demanded: CEC’s resignation, scrapping of assembly elections held over the last two years, suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and a return to paper ballots.“We urge you to take cognisance of this grave situation and use your good offices to ensure that the following demands are addressed without delay,” the memorandum read, listing four demands, including the restoration of 13.30 crore voters allegedly deleted from electoral rolls.The memorandum added: “We approach you because, in moments when every other door has been closed, the people of India look to the Office of the President as the final guardian of that covenant...”After meeting Murmu, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said he had expected the President to deny that vote theft was taking place but was surprised by her response.“I expected President to deny that 'vote chori' is taking place; I was shocked, stunned that she accepted what we said,” Rahul said.He also announced that opposition leaders would approach the Supreme Court on Monday. “We will go to Supreme Court on Monday to meet Chief Justice of India and hand over memorandum to him,” he said.The delegation included Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee, Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah and leaders from other INDIA bloc parties.Earlier, Opposition MPs marched from Parliament House towards Vijay Chowk carrying a “Save Democracy” banner but were stopped by police barricades.The latest action follows several days of protests against Gyanesh Kumar.

Opposition MPs marched from Parliament House towards Vijay Chowk carrying a ‘Save Democracy’ banner but were stopped by police barricades. Article Title: 2026 bypoll results: Vijay’s TVK sweeps Tamil Nadu, BJP wins Bengal, Assam
Article Text:
Bypoll results in Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Assam and Puducherry

Tamil Nadu: Vijay’s TVK expands its footprint

West Bengal: BJP’s march continues

Assam and Puducherry: Ruling parties hold ground

NEW DELHI: Ruling parties in their respective states continued to hold their ground as votes were counted in the bypolls on Friday, October 9.In Tamil Nadu, it was still “Thalapathy” Vijay and his TVK brigade making their presence felt. In West Bengal, the BJP strengthened its position, while in Assam, the saffron party maintained its comfortable lead. Puducherry, meanwhile, remained firmly with chief minister N Rangaswamy's ruling AINRC.Tamil Nadu and West Bengal went to bypolls in two assembly constituencies each, months after their assembly elections brought new parties to power in both states.Vijay’s TVK won both Madurantakam and Dharapuram, expanding its footprint in a state long dominated by Dravidian giants.TVK’s K Maragatham Kumaravel defeated DMK’s I Paranthamen in Madurantakam by 17,554 votes, while Sathyabama P defeated DMK’s Suganya in Dharapuram by 10,196 votes.Both constituencies had voted for the AIADMK in the previous Assembly elections, making TVK’s performance another sign of its growing electoral presence.TVK chief and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday celebrated the party's clean sweep in the Maduranthakam and Dharapuram Assembly by-elections.Framing the results as a historic rejection of money-power politics, Vijay in a post on X asserted that the voters have delivered a resounding verdict in favour of principled democracy, political civility, and individual dignity."The by-election results for Maduranthakam and Dharapuram have been announced. The top position reflecting the primary strength that the people hold in their hearts for our Tamil Nadu Victory League, and the deep subconscious desire of our own people for our conscientious democracy, have once again been proven," he wrote on X.The BJP, meanwhile, showed no signs of slowing down, winning both Nandigram and Rejinagar.In Nandigram, BJP candidate Hasi Rani Rath defeated Congress’s Milan Pradhan by a record margin of 1,22,753 votes in a constituency closely associated with chief minister Suvendu Adhikari’s political journey. Rath polled 1,64,427 votes against Pradhan’s 41,674.Suvendu has won Nandigram in the last three consecutive assembly elections. In 2016, he was a close confidant of then-chief minister Mamata Banerjee. He later broke away from the TMC, joined the BJP and emerged as one of her fiercest political rivals.He has now succeeded former boss Mamata as chief minister of Bengal.In Rejinagar, BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar also won, marking a breakthrough for the party in the Muslim-majority constituency.Sakharav Sarkar was declared winner by a massive margin of 75,816 votes on Friday. While Sarkar secured 1,29,914 votes, Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP)'s Golam Nabi Azad came in the second position securing 54,098 votes.The Bengal CM claimed that the BJP had secured around 60% of Muslim votes in Rejinagar and 80% in Nandigram."Minority community found friend in BJP, voted for us in bypolls," Bengal CM Suvendu said after muslim-dominated Rejinagar supported the saffron party in big numbers.In Assam, the BJP appeared firmly placed in the contest for the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat, which fell vacant and went to a bypoll.BJP candidate Devasish Sharma won by 1,42,224 votes over AIUDF chief Badruddin Ajmal as counting continues. Though the BJP candidate's victory is now imminent.Sharma polled 7,14,349 votes, while Ajmal secured 5,72,125 votes. Congress nominee Sibamoni Bora was a distant third with 75,908 votes. Counting was still underway.Puducherry, meanwhile, delivered a win for the ruling side, with chief minister N Rangaswamy’s party securing the Thattanchavady seat. AINRC candidate Ashok Anand defeated Congress rival E Vinayagam by over 8,400 votes.Union home minister Amit Shah on Friday hailed the National Democratic Alliance's victories in by-elections in West Bengal, Assam and Puducherry, along with recent municipal elections in Rajasthan and Tripura, saying these wins indicate that people have "completely rejected" the INDI alliance.In a post on X, Shah said, "Despite the lies, confusion, and malicious propaganda of Rahul Gandhi and the INDI Alliance, the BJP is winning one election after another under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership.""Having lost their public support, these parties question institutions after every defeat, but the people have recognized this character of theirs. That is why, once again, they have expressed their unwavering faith in the BJP by giving it a resounding mandate," he further said.
Article Summary: Vijay’s TVK won both Madurantakam and Dharapuram, expanding its footprint in a state long dominated by Dravidian giants. In West Bengal, the BJP strengthened its position, while in Assam, the saffron party maintained its comfortable lead. Puducherry remained firmly with chief minister N Rangaswamy's ruling AINRC.

Article Title: 'Unwarranted, offensive': India slams US Vice President JD Vance 'indentured servants' amid H-1B visa row

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday slammed US vice-president JD Vance over his description of H-1B visa workers as "indentured servants", calling his remarks "unwarranted" and "deeply offensive".In a statement, responding to Vance’s comments, the ministry said, "We have also seen some comments in this context by the US Vice President. We believe that such descriptions are unwarranted and ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem."The MEA also highlighted the contribution of immigrants to the US economy, saying, "Indeed, the history of the United States itself has been shaped by generations of immigrants whose labour, enterprise and innovation have contributed to its growth and prosperity.""Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive," it added.Vance made the remarks while addressing a news conference on visa fraud, alleging that companies bring in foreign workers at lower wages while laying off American employees.“If you are working as an H-1B visa in the United States of America, you’re earning $20,000 less than an American citizen hired in the same position.If you were brought in by one of these foreign outsourcing firms, you’re making $48,000 less than an American citizen in a similar position," Vance said."So, I’m sure that everybody here understands the game that is being played. You bring in indentured servants from outside the country, you lay off American workers and, if you’re a corporation, you make a ton of money by under cutting the wages of American workers, replacing them with people who frankly shouldn’t be in the United States of America to begin with,” he added.The MEA said that it was aware of the US department of labor’s decision concerning the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme for certain companies."It should also be clear that talent mobility adds value to both economies. While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US," the statement said."This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact. The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries,” it added.The MEA also clarified that PERM is separate from the H-1B visa programme. It said the suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of visa holders and their dependents, although it could affect the green card process for eligible employees of the companies concerned.“We continue to follow developments around this issue,” the ministry added.The MEA’s response came a day after the Trump administration suspended eight companies, TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Cognizant, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe, from participating in the PERM programme.The US administration’s move is part of a broader crackdown on skilled-worker immigration. US officials have alleged that companies have used the system at the expense of American workers.The US department of labor said it would stop accepting and processing new and pending PERM applications involving the affected companies.PERM is an important step in the employment-based green card process. Employers generally need labour certification from the US department of labor before sponsoring eligible foreign workers for permanent residence.The process requires employers to establish that there are not enough qualified, willing and available US workers for a position and that hiring a foreign worker will not adversely affect wages and working conditions.
Article Summary: US vice-president JD Vance described H-1B visa workers as 'indentured servants' The ministry of external affairs called his remarks "unwarranted" and "deeply offensive" Vance made the remarks while addressing a news conference on visa fraud.

Article Title: ‘Nuclear weapons not routine instruments of statecraft’: India’s warning to Pakistan at UN
Article Text:
‘India will not bow to nuclear blackmail’: New Delhi hits back at Pakistan at UN (Anmol Sher Singh Bedi)

India reiterates three red lines

India raises Indus Waters Treaty, nuclear proliferation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India on Friday warned Pakistan against using nuclear weapons as a tool of political pressure, asserting that New Delhi would not bow to nuclear blackmail and that any terrorist attack against the country would invite a fitting response.Exercising its Right of Reply at the United Nations General Assembly's First Committee, which deals with disarmament and international security, India said nuclear weapons must not be treated as “routine instruments of statecraft”.Senior Adviser (Disarmament) at India's Permanent Mission to the Conference on Disarmament in Geneva, Anmol Sher Singh Bedi, delivered the response following remarks by Pakistan on Jammu and Kashmir.“Jammu and Kashmir is an integral and inalienable part of India,” Bedi said, rejecting Pakistan's claims over the region.He said India's military capabilities were defensive in nature and shaped by its security environment, rather than directed against any particular country.“We heard concerns about escalation. These are legitimate concerns. However, these are best judged by conduct over time. Nuclear weapons must not be treated as routine instruments of statecraft,” Bedi said.He warned that relying on the threat of nuclear weapons to shield activities below the threshold of conventional warfare could increase the risk of escalation rather than promote restraint.“A posture that relies on nuclear overhang to limit the consequences of subconventional activity raises the risk of escalation and not the prospect of restraint,” he said.Bedi also outlined what he described as a recurring pattern in regional crises, involving provocation, denial of responsibility and subsequent appeals for restraint after a response.“Where those in power are neither elected by people nor accountable to them, their decisions carry no risk and impose no cost for those who take them. That is how crisis becomes an instrument of power. That is how instability becomes useful, and that is how the cycle keeps on repeating,” he said.India said its position on terrorism and national security remained clear, identifying three principles that would guide its response to threats.“First, any terrorist attack against India will receive a fitting response. Second, India will not bow to nuclear blackmail. Third, India will make no distinction between those who sponsor terrorism and those who mastermind it,” Bedi said.He said India's actions in May 2025 followed a “grave provocation” and were undertaken in self-defence after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 civilians, mostly tourists, were killed.“These actions were measured, targeted, and designed to be non-escalatory,” Bedi said.India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, 2025, targeting what it described as terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir in retaliation for the Pahalgam attack. The Resistance Front, a proxy of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba, was linked to the attack.Bedi also stressed that the use of non-state actors by a country did not absolve it of responsibility for their actions.“The use of force by states under the garb of non-state actors does not erase the state's responsibility. India's right of self-defense remains intact,” he said.India also referred to the Indus Waters Treaty, arguing that the agreement depended on mutual trust and cooperation between the two countries.“A state cannot undermine those foundations of trust and cooperation and at the same time insist that the privileges flowing from the relationship remain untouched,” Bedi said.Following the Pahalgam attack, India announced that the treaty would be held in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably ended its support for cross-border and other forms of terrorism.On nuclear proliferation, Bedi invoked the legacy of Pakistani nuclear scientist Abdul Qadeer Khan and the international proliferation network associated with him, which supplied nuclear equipment and expertise to countries seeking to develop nuclear weapons.The network contributed to international concerns that led to United Nations Security Council Resolution 1540, adopted in 2004, which requires states to prevent the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their means of delivery to non-state actors.“This is relevant in the context of demands for unquestioned nuclear cooperation and transfer of advanced weapons and military capabilities. We urge all states and all responsible suppliers to exercise the highest degree of vigilance, not because of India, but for their own security,” Bedi said.
Article Summary: India warns Pakistan against using nuclear weapons as a tool of political pressure. New Delhi says any terrorist attack against the country would invite a fitting response. India says nuclear weapons must not be treated as ‘routine instruments of statecraft’

Article Title: Can’t stop metro & trains, act as situation unfolds: Supreme Court to govt
Article Text:

SC: Issue a traffic advisory so that people don’t suffer

‘Jantar Mantar as protest site needs to change’
