NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday ordered govt not to stop Delhi metro services and trains heading to the capital on Saturday due to law and order “concerns” related to the anti-SIR protest planned by CJP, but said public transport services could be regulated depending on how the situation unfolds.Responding to a plea challenging govt’s decision on metro and train operations, a CJI-headed bench said it would inconvenience people dependent on public transport, and secured an assurance fr­om the solicitor general that there would be no blanket ban on movement of metro and trains reaching Delhi Saturday.The hearing saw the SC bench drive home their concern about proportionality by using the popular Hindi expression on using a hammer to swat a fly. Cautioned by SG Tushar Mehta that his remark could be misinterpreted, the bench clarified that they did not use the expression literally.In terms of that assurance, we direct competent authorities to allow plying of metro and trains in an appropriately regulated manner so as not to inconvenience public at large, and such decision may be given wide publicity to ensure citizens are aware of availability of the services,” said the bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.“Similarly, appropriate traffic advisory is issued in newspapers and websites to enable people to avoid roads which are blocked and undertake travel inside the city. ”The bench focused on inconvenience likely to result from closure of public transport, and whether such a prohibition was required.Mehta had defended the su­spension of operations by te­rming it a regulated resp­o­nse to what he called an “em­e­r­ging law and order situation”.The urgent hearing that was allowed out of turn was marked by the absence of any challenge to Delhi Police’s denial of permission to CJP to hold an agitation against Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. “The only issue before us is whether the complete stoppage of metro and movement of trains requires reconsideration,” the judges told a team of senior advocates led by Kapil Sibal, who had sought the hearing.It was at 11.45am that the team of advocates made the mention in the interlude between two listed case hearings to complain that citizen’s fundamental right to peaceful protest was being strangled by orders of police and railways to shut down metro and rail services to Delhi.“How can this happen in our country,” Sibal asked and said he was appearing for CPM MP MA Baby. He was joined by senior advocates A M Singhvi, Prashant Bhushan, Vrinda Grover, Nithya Ramakrishna, N Hariharan and G Sankaranarayanan. The bench agreed to hear them but said someone from CJP, which has planned the protest, should appear. They held the urgent hearing despite CJP and other organisers of the protest not turning up at 2pm as promised by Sibal and the other advocates.SC asked Sibal and other counsel that “are any of you appearing for any of the organisers of the protest Saturday? Is Baby an organiser of the protest?” Sibal said his client was not an organiser. The bench asked have they sought permission to hold a protest. Bhushan responded they had sought permission much before but it was denied Friday morning.SC said the organisers needed to challenge the order of denial. “No doubt the right to form an association is a fundamental right, but that right must be exercised as per law. Once police deny permission, it needs to be challenged in court,” it said. “What is the ground reality with regard to protest? If it is with permission, it is a lawful protest. If it is not with permission, it is not in accordance with law. Even if it is not in accordance with law, we do not say people do not have a right to protest. But they are at the pain of prosecution,” the bench said.SG intervened to say CJP had in July sought permission to hold a day-long protest against the leak of NEET-UG papers, but stayed put at Jantar Mantar for 20 days.The bench kept its focus on the responsibility of organisers. “If we know who the organisers are, we can ask them what is the expected number of participants in the protest. We can regulate that and call upon the state to calibrate their responses not in a broad-spectrum way like complete stoppage of metro and rail service. But you say Baby is not an organiser,” the bench said.Sibal said, “I can come wi­th an organiser, but the court will say where is the order. By that time Oct 10 will be over. Allow us to represent an organiser and hear us at 2pm.” However, at 2pm, none of the organisers turned up.During the hearing, govt ag­r­eed with Sibal and other lawyers that the designated protest site needs to be ch­a­n­ged from Jantar Mantar to somewhere else. SG Mehta informed SC that he agreed wi­th their suggestions that govt soon take a decision to identify a designated protest venue instead of Jantar Mantar.The CJI-led bench said, “Govt and parties are agreeable to the suggestion that it is high time to identify and designate a proper protest site, instead of Jantar Mantar.... The competent authorities wo­uld consider the suggestion and take an appropriate decision.”
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders govt not to stop Delhi metro services and trains heading to the capital on Saturday due to law and order ‘concerns’ The bench said public transport services could be regulated depending on how the situation unfolds. The hearing saw the SC bench drive home their concern about proportionality by using the popular Hindi expression on using a hammer to swat a fly.

Article Title: ‘Obvious weakness’: Zelenskyy slams Trump’s Russian diesel deal, warns it could prolong war

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday (local time) warned that easing sanctions against Russia without a clear and lasting de-escalation agreement would be an “obvious weakness” that could prolong the war by allowing Moscow to continue selling petroleum products.In a post on X, Zelenskyy said peace could not be achieved through weakness and called for stronger sanctions, continued support for Ukraine and sustained pressure on Moscow to end the war."Peace never comes through weakness. Today, representatives of the US Congress were in Kyiv – a bipartisan delegation – and I am grateful to them for visiting Ukraine at such a difficult time. They asked: what is needed to end the war? The answer must be strong. There must be sanctions under the Lindsey Graham bill, there must be support for Ukraine in protecting lives, and there must be pressure on Russia for its war. And today, there was a conversation between the leaders of America and Russia. A conversation that leads to something different," he wrote.Referring to the diesel announcement, Zelenskyy said, “Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world.Russia will ‘repay’ the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged.""Recently, there was a European decision to lift sanctions on Russian oligarchs. Since then, Russian strikes and the torment of people have only increased," he added.Citing recent Russian attacks across Ukraine, Zelenskyy said, "This past week alone, there was a brutal Russian missile strike on a residential building in Pryluky, aerial bombs were dropped on Kramatorsk – on ordinary city buses – and there have been constant attacks on Kyiv’s energy infrastructure and on the life-sustaining infrastructure in Dnipro, Kharkiv, Odesa, and our other cities. Dozens of people have been killed and hundreds wounded. "He alleged that Russia was resorting to such attacks because it was struggling to achieve its objectives on the battlefield. "The Russians are compensating for their inability to achieve their objectives on the battlefield with this kind of terror. This year, Russia is weaker on the battlefield than at any other point in the war. That is why Putin is relying on terror. That is why he is relying on attempts to strike backroom deals to secure some form of pressure relief for Russia, in order to buy more time and more opportunities for war," he further said.Zelenskyy said Ukraine was prepared to take reciprocal steps towards de-escalation, adding that the American team was aware of Kyiv’s position."Ukraine is ready to take symmetrical de-escalatory steps, and the American team knows our position. Our strikes on Russian oil refineries and other oil facilities are a response to Russia’s years-long campaign of terror against Ukraine’s energy sector. Ukraine will not set Russian oil refineries on fire if Russia does not destroy our energy infrastructure. This is the kind of agreement we are proposing to America, and we believe the United States has enough power to achieve such a compromise," he said.Zelenskyy’s remarks came after US President Donald Trump spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin and announced a deal to secure diesel supplies from Russia, marking a shift in Washington’s pressure on Moscow over the war in Ukraine as the US seeks to address rising fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections.In a social media post on Friday, Trump said Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel, followed by another 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”. He added that Russia would deliver another 3 million tonnes “within a short period of time”.The announcement came just a month after Trump signed a sweeping Russia sanctions law aimed at curbing Moscow’s oil and gas revenues, which help fund its war against Ukraine.

Article Title: Turning scandal into spotlight
Article Text:
‘

Paths of Glory’. It became

In 2009, I met Jeffrey Archer at Landmark, Chennai, when he came to India to launchone of my favourite Archer novels, inspired by the real-life story of British mountaineer George Mallory and his mysterious disappearance on Everest. I had my copy signed by him and remember the fan-girl moment.From school to college, hardly a month passed without an Archer short story or novel finding its way into my hands. His narration had one unmistakable signature—the twist in the tale. Over more than five decades, he built a global readership, with his books published in 114 countries and more than 47 languages, selling over 300 million copies.I can recall at least ten stories where the final turn makes you levitate from your chair. When I asked Archer at Landmark how he managed to write “like a machine”, he smiled. A writer without discipline, he said, will perish. His day began at six, followed by five hours of writing, from 6.30am to 11.30am, without calls, visitors or family interruptions. After that, the day was his.I also asked which Indian English writer he admired. Without hesitation, he said, ‘ R K Narayan ’. Archer’s admiration for Narayan’s ability to bring Indian life alive through English was immediate.Mallory, the main character in ‘Paths of Glory’, disappeared on Everest in 1924 while attempting to reach the summit. Whether he became the first man to climb the Everest remains unknown. His body was discovered 75 years later, a few 100 metres below the summit. Among his belongings, one object was missing—the photograph of his wife, Ruth. Mallory had promised Ruth that if he reached the summit, he would leave her photograph there. Did he reach the top and keep his promise? Nobody knows.That is Archer at his finest: research, suspense, emotion and an unexpected clue, stitched together with the elegance of a master storyteller.Archer’s own life contained twists no novelist could resist. At the height of his fame, he was a parliamentarian and a close associate of Margaret Thatcher. After a newspaper accused him of paying a sex worker, he won a libel case in 1987. But it later emerged that he had lied in court. In 2001, he was sentenced to four years for perjury. His political career ended.But his story did not.In prison, he kept a 1,001 page journal, later published as ‘A Prison Diary’. After his release came ‘Cat O’Nine Tales’, stories inspired by fellow prisoners. Betrayal, justice and second chances began to echo through his writing.What fascinates me most is his alchemy: he turned disgrace into material, confinement into creativity and a public fall into a second literary ascent.Valluvar says in Kural 240:“Vasai Ozhiya Vaazhvaare VaazhvarIsaiyozhiya Vaazhvaare Vaazhadhavar.”“Those who live free of blame truly live; Those who live without renown have not truly lived.”Archer’s life complicates that wisdom. Here was a man who knew blame, disgrace and downfall—and yet transformed them into another kind of grace.Perhaps that is the most Archer-like twist of all: the story was not over with the fall. He simply turned the page.
Article Summary: Jeffrey Archer's books published in 114 countries and more than 47 languages, selling over 300 million copies. His narration had one unmistakable signature—the twist in the tale. At the height of his fame, he was a parliamentarian and close associate of Margaret Thatcher.

Article Title: Before CJP protest, Delhi bandh: Mobile net, metro, roads blocked in heart of city

NEW DELHI: Checks at Delhi’s borders and barricaded roads inside, mobile internet snapped and metro stations shut — Delhi Police has put in place stringent measures to stop protesters from gathering at Jantar Mantar on Saturday morning. Central Delhi looked like an impregnable fortress by Friday night.The fortified city is expected to see around 35,000 security personnel, including those from Delhi Police and paramilitary forces, to stop what the authorities estimate will be a crowd of 20,000 from reaching Jantar Mantar. The protest is scheduled to start at 10am. Police sources said extra forces were requested because the gathering during the Cockroach Janta Party protest in June-July had been “underestimated”.Mobile internet services in a 4km radius from the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing were snapped at 10pm on Friday. The curbs will continue till 10pm on Saturday. Entry and exit at 57 metro stations (later reduced to 45) were stopped till further notice, after Delhi Police’s Transport Range wrote to Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, citing the possibility of “unruly crowd movement towards sensitive locations”.Apart from this, more than 30 blockade points — including some at the borders — have been identified.“Those attempting to create anarchy or move towards the protest site will be detained immediately. The plan is to stop them at the city’s borders,” an officer said.Joint CP Nupur Prasad said CJP submitted its request to hold a protest on Saturday at “very short notice” and hence permission could not be granted. The application was received on Oct 7. “As per the prescribed guidelines, such applications must be submitted at least 10 days before the protest,” she said.Referring to the June-July protests, JCP Nupur Prasad said, “On an earlier occasion, when CJP was granted permission to hold a protest, they failed to follow lawful directions and adhere to the undertakings they had submitted. Consequently, in view of their failure to comply with legal directions and undertakings, and considering the current requirements for maintaining public safety, law and order and traffic regulations, permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar has been denied. ”CJP co-convener Saurav Das, however, said the police had known about the protest since Oct 2 when they had announced it. The 10-day timeline is to ensure that adequate security forces are deployed and traffic arrangements are made, he said, pointing out that even before Oct 2, forces had been deployed as other outfits were protesting on the same issue.“This shows that all of this is an excuse. And we vehemently disagree with the very concept of seeking ‘permission’ from govt to protest against it. It’s absurd and doesn’t make any sense. It’s a colonial mindset,” he said.Personnel at some entry points have been asking motorists about their destinations to keep a check on any movement towards central Delhi.Joint Commissioner of Police (Northern Range) Madhur Verma posted on X Friday: “Prepare for the storm. Practise restraint. Protect the peace. Because the true strength of the police is not merely in controlling a crowd, but in doing so with discipline, dignity and minimum force.”Delhi Police also posted an open letter to citizens on X Friday, invoking duty and humanity, asking people to remember that police personnel have families too.An AI-generated image of a postcard appeared with the message: “Aapki awaaz aapka haq hai, aur aapki suraksha hamara farz. Uniform ke peeche bhi ek insaan hai, jiska apna parivar hai, apne log hain. Faraq sirf uniform ka hai, insaaniyat ka nahi (Your voice is your right, and your safety is our duty. Behind the uniform is a person who has a family and own people. The only difference is the uniform, not humanity).”In a detailed note, Delhi Police justified the curbs put in place: “The right to peaceful protest is an important democratic right. At the same time, New Delhi houses important establishments and offices of constitutional authorities and the safety and convenience of residents, workers, commuters and businesses must also be protected.Delhi Police is responsible for safeguarding all these interests while maintaining public order,” it said.“The circumstances surrounding the protests held at Jantar Mantar in July must be taken into consideration. Permission had reportedly been granted for a one-day protest, but the gathering continued for approximately a month. During this period, more than 200 police personnel were injured and over 2,000 individuals with criminal antecedents reportedly participated in the protests, contributing to incidents of violence. As the situation escalated, clashes occurred, resulting in injuries to innocent students as well,” it added.
Article Summary: Police sources say extra forces were requested because the gathering during the Cockroach Janta Party protest in June-July had been “underestimated” Mobile internet services in a 4km radius from the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing were snapped at 10pm on Friday. Entry and exit at 57 metro stations (later reduced to 45) were stopped till further notice.

NEW DELHI: Tax authorities in Bengaluru have come across a new tool for evading taxes and stamp duty, a development that may have implications across states. Initial estimates suggest land deals of over Rs 300 crore have seen under-reporting.The income tax department's directorate of intelligence and criminal investigation in the southern city has found several instances of incomplete disclosure of the entire sale consideration in the registered sale deeds.The remaining amount is paid by executing unregistered full and final settlement deeds with the payment routed through banking channels.There are several instances of the method being used by local builders to purchase land parcels and then develop them into residential units and plots."Since the additional payment made is not part of the sale deed, the buyer pays no stamp duty and registration fee to the state govt, resulting in huge revenue loss," said a person familiar with the probe.The tax authorities have alerted the registration department in Karnataka. Stamp duty evasion in the state can result in hefty penalties.Besides, the buyers did not deduct TDS despite purchasing 'urban agricultural land' as a result of which the additional amount paid through full and final settlement deed remained outside the radar of the tax department.Some of the sellers, who have claimed exemption from the sale of agricultural land have not filed their returns, as a result of which tax was not paid."The department also identified a number of registered transactions involving exchange of property involving undervaluation of properties sold, on which there is short payment of stamp duty and registration fee and payment of additional consideration outside the book," said a person in the know.The findings call for a revision in the guidance value of the land which is adjacent to urban areas and align the prices to market rates."The circle rate is significantly lower than the market rate, which is resulting in these kind of transactions," an official said.
Article Summary: Tax authorities in Bengaluru have come across a new tool for evading taxes and stamp duty. Initial estimates suggest land deals of over Rs 300 crore have seen under-reporting. There are several instances of the method being used by local builders to purchase land parcels and then develop them.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Friday refused to entertain an AIADMK party worker's petition challenging the Tamil Nadu speaker's decision to accept AIADMK's plea to withdraw disqualification petitions against 21 of its legislators who had defied party orders and voted for the confidence motion moved by the governing TVK.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said when the party, to which the MLAs belonged, has condoned the lapse and withdrawn its petitions seeking their disqualification, a person who is not even an MLA cannot challenge the speaker's decision.The petitioner said that by their very conduct, the 25 MLAs, of whom four have resigned, have indulged in anti-party activity and are liable for disqualification under the anti-defection law.The Supreme Court bench said in a multi-party democracy like India, political dynamics in a coalition govt must be left to the political parties and decisions in this regard by the speaker, unless palpably unconstitutional, cannot be interfered with by the courts.The Madras high court had earlier dismissed the appellant's writ petition against the speaker's order dropping disqualification proceedings against the 21 MLAs.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court Friday refused to entertain an AIADMK party worker's petition challenging the Tamil Nadu speaker's decision. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said when the party, to which the MLAs belonged, has condoned the lapse and withdrawn its petitions seeking their disqualification, a person who is not even an MLA cannot challenge the speaker's Decision.

Article Title: Judge recuses from Punjab government appeal case
Article Text:
SC: Thousand sources... don’t now where attacks will come

NEW DELHI: Justice Sheel Nagu, who was chief justice of Punjab and Haryana HC for nearly two years prior to his elevation to Supreme Court , on Friday recused from hearing Punjab govt's appeal against the HC's order directing a CBI probe into an alleged bribe syndicate, having links with the CM's OSD, that influenced postings, transfers and tenders.At the commencement of hearing, Justice Dipankar Datta said Justice Nagu wants to recuse from the case, even though senior advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Punjab govt, said the state did not have any objection to him remaining a part of the bench.Hinting that Justice Nagu’s continuation on the bench might be turned into a controversy, Justice Datta said, “These days there are a thousand sources. We do not know where the attacks will come.” In the recent past, AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal had raised questions about a Delhi HC judge’s impartiality and sought her recusal from hearing an appeal related to a criminal case against him.When Gupta reiterated his request, Justice Datta said SC has 17 benches and the case could go to another. The order stated: “Re-list this petition before a bench of which JusticeNagu is not a member.”
Article Summary: Justice Sheel Nagu was chief justice of Punjab and Haryana HC for nearly two years prior to his elevation to Supreme Court. Punjab govt's appeal against HC's order directing a CBI probe into an alleged bribe syndicate that influenced postings, transfers and tenders.
